description: Threads as conversations (spec 9.2, 9.3). Each case is the copy of one thread that Ana's home broker keeps: turns by ana are sent by Ana's agent (direction out), turns by lee are received (direction in), all in the case's scope between alp:ana@example.org and alp:lee@example.org, applied in order at their `at`. A turn names the message it answers by the id of an earlier turn in `in_reply_to` (an id no accepted turn has means the broker doesn't hold it), or names none (a follow-up). `status` is an ack's status; `terms` stands for the terms_hash an accept or commit carries; `ratified` lists whose ratification records the broker holds when a commit is evaluated, and the commit references them; they are valid until `ratified_until` when it is given, otherwise until after the case. A thread takes at most 200 messages besides one that ends it. A refused turn changes nothing. expected.state is the thread's state after the turn as the broker reports it at that turn's `at` (null: no thread yet). Every turn is a full message besides: its policy checks are the policy vectors' business; here the thread rules decide, and, for a turn that carries a `body`, the scope's semantic rules (spec 7.8): in alp.availability/1, each free interval of an inform lies inside the window of the request it answers, when that request is its recipient's, or otherwise of the latest request its recipient sent (refused with schema_invalid).

cases.name: alp.status/1: an update answered by an update, an added update, a follow-up question and its answer, a question back, closed by an ack
alp.briefing/1: a clarifying question back and its answer, the briefing, an added point, a follow-up question declined without ending the conversation, closed by an ack
alp.briefing/1: a decline of the thread's first message closes it, whichever side declines
alp.availability/1: follow-up questions and answers; the replies map decides what answers what; an ack that says received leaves the thread open
alp.availability/1: every free interval lies inside the window its recipient asked about, whether the inform answers that request, updates an answer or follows up
alp.availability/1: free intervals answer a question; an inform when its recipient has asked nothing is refused
alp.briefing/1: a thread starts only with a type in starts and replies to nothing; a reply names a message the broker holds; types that must reply can't follow up
alp.status/1: every message keeps the thread open for its own lifetime; once the latest has expired the thread is expired
alp.status/1: a thread takes at most 200 messages; then only a message that ends it
alp.meeting/1: a request answered by a request before any proposal; nothing conversational while terms are open or agreed; the ratified commit; informs both ways after it
alp.meeting/1: an accept or a counter answers the other party's latest proposal, never the sender's own or one a later proposal replaced
alp.meeting/1: agreed terms end with a commit, a decline or expiry: an ack can't close them, and acknowledgements and errors don't prolong them
alp.meeting/1: a commit needs both ratification records still valid; a decline then cancels the terms
alp.document_request/1: the request clarified both ways; propose answers a request (it doesn't start these threads); only the proposer commits; informs after the commit
alp.meeting/1: a decline after agreement cancels the terms, and nothing more is accepted
alp.meeting/1: a committed thread doesn't expire; it stays open for reports until either side closes it
